name: Bygone Bishop
oracle_text:
Flying
Whenever you cast a creature spell with mana value 3 or less, investigate. (Create a Clue token. It's an artifact with "{2}, Sacrifice this token: Draw a card.")
blocked_sentences: Whenever you cast a creature spell with mana value 3 or less, investigate. (Create a Clue token. It's an artifact with "{2}, Sacrifice this token: Draw a card.")

Scope: only the `investigate` half of this one printed line is blocked, and it is blocked on a single missing thing -- a Clue token in the shared token pool. The trigger half IS expressible today and needs nothing new; see `expressible_today` below. Because the residual gate reads a printed line as a whole, and because a trigger that fires and creates nothing is a strictly worse card than the one printed (Bygone Bishop's entire function is the Clues), the line goes here rather than being written half. The card already in the hand-written pool covers none of it: `data/cards/isperia.cards.json` has it as a vanilla 2/3 flier -- and with mana cost `{2}{W}{W}` where the packet and the printing say `{2}{W}`, which wants fixing when this is implemented.

needs.what: a Clue token definition in the shared token pool -- one new object in `data/cards/tokens.cards.json`, e.g. id `clue_token`, name `Clue`, `types: ["Artifact"]`, `subtypes: ["Clue"]`, `is_token: true`, no mana cost, no colors, and a single activated ability `{"kind": "activated", "text": "{2}, Sacrifice this artifact: Draw a card.", "cost": {"mana": "{2}", "sacrifice": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "self_only": true, "count": 1}}, "effects": [{"op": "draw", "player": "you", "amount": {"const": 1}}]}`. Every piece of that ability is already supported -- `Cost` carries both `mana` and a `sacrifice` selector (`engine/carddef.py:37-49`), and the `self_only` sacrifice-self shape is used by three cards in `data/cards/aesi.cards.json` and `data/cards/core.cards.json` -- so this is a data addition with no engine change behind it. With it in the pool, `investigate` is spelled `{"op": "create_token", "token": "clue_token", "amount": {"const": 1}}` and needs no new op.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `create_token` is in the vocabulary and can name any token id, but `validate_token_references` (`cards/loader.py:683-693`) raises `DslError` unless that id resolves to a card already in the registry with `is_token` set -- it is checked by `CardRegistry.from_paths` and again by gate 3 of the authoring verifier (`cards/authoring/verify.py:420-429`), so naming a Clue that nobody has defined is a load-time failure, not a silent no-op. `data/cards/tokens.cards.json` holds 16 tokens and none is a Clue; `treasure_token` is the closest and the only non-creature among them, which is why it is worth naming: it proves an artifact token with an activated ability loads and works, but its ability adds mana and its cost is `{"tap": true}` -- a different cost, a different effect and a different subtype, so it cannot stand in for a Clue. A card worker cannot supply the definition either: an answer file is exactly one `{"card": ..., "expectation": ...}` pair and `read_answers` (`cards/authoring/packet.py:221-238`) keys it by that one card's id, and `data/cards/` is off-limits to workers -- so the token has to be added by whoever does this work, not by the card that uses it. Adding it unblocks every investigate card at once, not just this one.

expressible_today.note: Recorded so nobody re-derives it. The trigger needs no new vocabulary and should be written exactly this way once the Clue exists.
expressible_today.why_it_works: `spell_cast` is in `TRIGGER_EVENTS` and is in `OBJECT_SUBJECT_TRIGGERS` (`engine/triggers.py:50-65`), so the event's `spell_oid` becomes the subject a `filter` is matched against (`_subject_oid`, line 248-255). `matches_card_filter` reads `mana_value` off the printed card face at line 325-326, comparing through `_compare` with the same `{"op", "value"}` shape the selector language uses -- so "a creature spell with mana value 3 or less" is one filter, not two questions. `controller: "you"` is compared against `event.player` for `spell_cast` (`_actor`, line 262-263), which is the caster, and that is what "whenever YOU cast" means.
expressible_today.expectation_if_it_were_written: `{"zone": "battlefield", "battlefield_count": 33}` -- nothing casts a spell after the card under test in the verification sandbox, so this trigger cannot fire there and no `tokens` assertion would be honest even with the Clue defined.
